beats.title: The Abandoned Camp
beats.boundaryReason: The session opens with the party surveying the ruined fort and investigating the disturbed campsite outside its walls; the beat ends when they decide to cross the causeway and scout inside.
dateEvidence: The session manifest dates the session to 1748-03-25.
At u0218-u0219 the DM says the party left first thing in the morning and reached the fort in the mid-to-late morning.

beats.title: Ambush in the Fort
beats.boundaryReason: Wellby's scouting draws the party into the fort's central ruin, where an ankheg erupts beneath him; the beat ends with Delwath killing it.
dateEvidence: This follows directly from the morning campsite investigation without a rest or day transition.
The session manifest dates the session to 1748-03-25.

beats.title: Aftermath and Burrow
beats.boundaryReason: After the ankheg dies, the party examines its burrow and the animal traffic below the headquarters, then turns toward the pentagonal building for shelter and a rest.
dateEvidence: This immediately follows the ankheg fight on the manifest date.
At u0855 the party proposes having lunch and taking a short rest.

beats.title: Temple and Towers
beats.boundaryReason: The party explores the Dunmari temple, rests, and searches the entrance towers, ending after they recover a magical horn and decide to descend underground.
dateEvidence: At u1111 the DM states that it is early afternoon.
The session manifest dates the session to 1748-03-25.

beats.title: The Statue and Coin
beats.boundaryReason: The party descends into the tunnels, finds a lifelike stone explorer, and experiments with a heavy golden coin that becomes a floating disc; the beat ends as they reform their marching order.
dateEvidence: This follows directly from the early-afternoon tower search with no rest or time transition.
The session manifest dates the session to 1748-03-25.

beats.title: The Cockatrice Nursery
beats.boundaryReason: Continuing through the narrow branch, the party discovers young cockatrices repeatedly petrifying a lion, retreats, and chooses the other passage.
dateEvidence: This is continuous with the afternoon tunnel exploration and contains no rest or day transition.
The session manifest dates the session to 1748-03-25.

beats.title: Beneath the Cistern
beats.boundaryReason: The party takes the wider branch beneath the ruined cistern, pauses to reason through the fort's history and the obsidian signal, and presses toward a larger cavern.
dateEvidence: At u1802 the DM describes midafternoon sunlight entering through the cistern.
The session manifest dates the session to 1748-03-25.

beats.title: Skeletons in the Dark
beats.boundaryReason: A hostile compulsion and three descending skeletons begin the cavern battle; the beat ends as a second threat enters from the far passage.
dateEvidence: The battle begins immediately after the party's midafternoon approach through the cistern passage.
The session manifest dates the session to 1748-03-25.

beats.title: The Obsidian Bearer
beats.boundaryReason: An undead hobgoblin carrying a darkness-wreathed obsidian staff joins the fight, which ends when Kenzo strikes it down and the staff clatters free.
dateEvidence: This is the uninterrupted second phase of the cavern battle on the manifest date.
No rest or time transition separates it from beat-008.

beats.title: Secrets of the Staff
beats.boundaryReason: After the battle, the party studies the undead and its still-hostile obsidian staff, identifies a flaw in the crystal, and debates where it can safely be destroyed.
dateEvidence: This follows immediately after the cavern battle without a rest or day transition.
The session manifest dates the session to 1748-03-25.

beats.title: Shattering the Obsidian
beats.boundaryReason: The party destroys the obsidian despite its psychic defenses, sees the surrounding beasts calm, then rests overnight in the temple and returns toward camp the next morning.
dateEvidence: The destruction follows directly from the same-day afternoon investigation.
At u3054-u3064 the party takes a long rest, wakes in the morning, and heads back toward camp, implying 1748-03-26.
